sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Western blot detection of HA-tagged ASGR2 confirms expression of the tagged full-length construct; no surface-specific assay (e.g. flow cytometry, surface biotinylation) or quantitative functional readout is reported in the ledger clips.
sites.rationale: ASGR2 is a type II single-pass transmembrane protein (N-terminus intracellular residues 1–55, TM 56–74, C-terminus extracellular 75–311). The C-terminus is therefore the sole extracellular terminus, making it the only position consistent with a C-terminal tag on the extracellular face. Python verification confirms residue 311 is 'A' (residue_before) and lies 237 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint. No residue number is named in any ledger clip, so position is topology_derived rather than validated. L2 and L3 describe the same construct in additional cell lines and are subsumed by L1. Full-length human ASGR2 subcloned into pcDNA 3.1 with a C-terminal HA tag; expressed in HepG2-PCSK9-KO and HEK293 cells and detected by western blot with HA-HRP antibody. No residue number is stated; 'C-terminal' is the only positional descriptor.

sources.claim: Human ASGR1 and its mutants (Q240A/W244A and Q240A/W244A/E253A) and human ASGR2 were subcloned into pcDNA 3.1 vector (Invitrogen) containing a C-terminal Flag tag (ASGR1) or HA tag (ASGR2).

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) describe the identical C-terminal HA-tagged ASGR2 construct from PMC8479480; they are not separate sites. No internal extracellular loop insertions, N-terminal tags, or other tag modalities are reported for ASGR2 in the ledger. The N-terminus (residues 1–55) is intracellular and therefore not a surface-tag candidate. Validation is detected_only because the ledger clips report only western blot detection; no flow cytometry, surface biotinylation, or quantitative functional assay result is captured in the clips.
